# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan, 2024: initial evidence note

Scope: broad web pass using primary and highly credible sources where available. I did not inspect repository materials. Question IDs below are best-fit inferred families, not canonical sub-IDs.

| Period | Valence | Claim title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs (inferred) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Background | Critical | Pakistan’s economy slowed sharply in FY23; reforms were needed for stability and growth | World Bank | 2023-10-03 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/10/02/fiscal-reforms-are-critical-for-economic-stability-sustainable-growth-in-pakistan | Background context, not a 2024 event: the World Bank says Pakistan entered 2024 after a FY23 contraction, with pressure from floods, import controls, political uncertainty, high prices, and weak confidence. | 8B.* |
| 2024 | Mixed | Pakistan stalemate ends, Sharif’s party seeks to get partner PPP to join cabinet | Reuters | 2024-02-14 | https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-stalemate-ends-sharifs-party-seeks-to-get-partner-ppp-to-join-cabinet/1965982/ | After the February election produced a hung parliament, Sharif was chosen to lead a coalition effort. This supports a reading of his return as negotiated and politically fragile rather than mandate-driven. | 7.*, 8B.* |
| 2024 | Mixed | Pakistan’s Shehbaz Sharif takes oath as prime minister, directs team to talk with IMF | Reuters | 2024-03-04 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/pakistans-shehbaz-sharif-takes-oath-as-prime-minister-3322834 | Sharif was sworn in on March 4 and immediately pushed his team toward IMF engagement, showing that economic stabilization was the first-order agenda of the new term. | 8B.* |
| 2024 | Mixed | Pakistan: IMF reaches staff-level agreement on the second and final review of the 9-month SBA | IMF | 2024-03-20 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/19/pr2491-pakistan-imf-reaches-staff-level-agreement-second-final-review-9-month-sba | The IMF said the new government intended to continue stabilization and reform, while also warning that growth would remain modest, inflation was still well above target, and major vulnerabilities persisted. | 8B.* |
| 2024 | Critical | Pakistan: Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/ | Amnesty condemned the election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a rights violation, indicating a coercive and rights-constrained election environment around Sharif’s ascent. | 7.* |
| 2024 | Favorable | IMF Executive Board approves 37-month EFF for Pakistan; growth returned and inflation declined | IMF | 2024-09-27 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr | The IMF credited the authorities with restoring stability: growth returned, external pressures eased, reserves doubled over the prior year, and inflation declined markedly, even as reforms remained required. | 8B.* |
| 2024 | Mixed | Pakistan’s economy stabilized in FY24, but poverty still rose | World Bank | 2024-10-10 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank | The World Bank said FY24 growth recovered to 2.5% and macro conditions improved, but poverty still increased and continued reform implementation was necessary. | 8B.* |

## Bottom line

2024 for Shehbaz Sharif looks like a term defined by:
- a shaky political start after an inconclusive election,
- immediate dependence on IMF stabilization,
- some macroeconomic improvement by late 2024,
- but continued poverty, reform dependence, and serious rights concerns around the election period.
